settings_help.source: (bool) - What happens to the original image files once their pixels are in fov.ome.zarr. On (the default): after each field is committed to fov.ome.zarr and every channel plane is verified byte for byte against its original, that field's originals are moved into orig/ in the project folder. Off: each original is deleted, but only after that same check passed for its field; this saves the disk space of a second copy and cannot be undone. A field whose channel was projected from several files (z slices) has no single plane to compare, so its originals are moved to orig/ even when this is off. A run cut short never loses an image: the next run checks again and finishes the moves or deletions. With mask_image_format 'npy' or 'tiff', or a timelapse run, the originals go to orig/ and are deleted at the end only when this is off, as before. save_original_images off or delete_intermediate on also turn keeping off. Default True.

(bool) - The older switch for the original images. Off acts as keep_original_images off: with fov.ome.zarr each original is deleted only after its field is committed and verified there; with 'npy', 'tiff' or timelapse runs the raw images are deleted once they are in stack/, as before, which is not reversible. Use keep_original_images instead. Default True.

(bool) - When the source folder holds images of several plates (read from the file names by the Mask filename pattern), move each plate's images into its own folder inside the source folder, then analyse each plate folder as its own project with its own fov.ome.zarr; run them together with the Batch Runner if you like. The run first prints a dry-run list (and writes all of it to spacr_plate_split_plan.tsv), never overwrites a file, and checks every file's size and each folder's file count after the moves. Off (the default): a folder of several plates stops the run with that list and nothing is moved. The GUI asks before it splits. Default False.
